# Vanishing scaled surface logarithms from contact gradients and a uniform trace inequality

This is a bounded consequence of the already proved SAME-separator volume
identities. It removes the logarithmic boundary term in the small-buffer
physical dual. It does not prove a Gamma cap-payment inequality.

The initial probe was common inner parallel erosion, an archived actual
motion. That motion alone only bounds the total negative boundary logarithm.
The stronger conclusion below uses the gradient labels of the very same
volume certificate and uniform interiority of its source marks. the contributor supplied
the decisive gradient/trace argument; Slab and Defect independently checked it.

Dependencies are:

* `candidate 79036a0d1b9e182a`, the
  concurrently saved parent proof of the decisive gradient/trace mechanism;
* `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`,
  especially (13)--(14), including its actual-cone/continuation hypotheses;
* `candidate ed103e599726c87f`
  for the exact upper bound Delta<=epsilon S_max;
* `candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96`
  for uniform source interiority and the bounded scaled parameter in the
  specified compact minimal-bad-body framework.

The last framework is an explicit premise, not a consequence of a bad value
on an arbitrary fixed base. No polytopal or regular-cap minimizer is assumed.

## 1. Precise data and the same-certificate identity

Let P be a fixed finite base, with compatible positive convex fibers K_z in
R^d, N=d+1, mixed volume dm, and M=sum_z |K_z|. Work along a sequence with
epsilon down to zero. Suppose there are uniform constants

    K_z subset B(0,R),  B(o_z,r_b) subset K_z,
    M>=M_*,  lambda_min(Sigma)>=lambda_*>0.

Let L=min_r A_r be a positive finite-PL concave parameter, positive on a
neighborhood of the canonical hull and normalized by

    integral_S log L dm=0.

The positive contact coefficients of the common physical/parameter dual are
e_a, with Delta=sum_a e_a>0, source marks Y_a=(p_a,y_a), values L_a=L(Y_a),
and unique continuous gradients c_a at these positive sources. Repeated
occurrences of the same mark may be merged or retained. Assume

    B(y_a,r_s) subset K_(p_a)                         (1)

with r_s>0 uniform. The gradient uniqueness is a consequence of the contact
martingale, not an assumption used to create that martingale. On each open
PL cell write c(w)=grad_X L(w). The audited identity is, for every bounded
function chi on the finite set of continuous gradients,

    (Delta/M) integral_S chi(c(w))/L(w) dm
         =sum_a e_a chi(c_a)/L_a.                    (2)

It remains valid in the nonregular, multicontact construction: e_a are the
SAME coefficients occurring in the physical density, including its common
supporting-facet selections. A separately chosen parameter-only certificate
cannot be substituted in (2).

Put

    kappa=Delta/(NM),  B(w)=-kappa log L(w).

Here kappa is the scalar logarithmic coefficient, not a group coarea weight.
Assume the already proved quantitative inputs

    Delta<=epsilon S_max,
    L_max:=max_S L<=H epsilon^(-N)                    (3)

for fixed S_max,H. Increasing H to at least one is harmless. Uniform
vanishing of epsilon^N L is stronger than the second assertion of (3), but
is not needed in the estimates below.

## 2. Exact volume gradient and volume L1 bounds

Choose any active affine majorant A at Y_a. Its continuous gradient is c_a,
and A(Y_a)=L_a. Positivity on the source ball (1) gives

    0<A(p_a,y_a-r_s c_a/|c_a|)=L_a-r_s |c_a|

when c_a is nonzero. Thus |c_a|/L_a<=1/r_s. This argument needs no bound on
the base coefficients of A and remains valid at a boundary base.

At each fixed pair the gradient labels form a finite set. Consequently
chi(c)=|c| is a legitimate bounded test in (2), even if its maximum is not
uniform along the sequence. Since L is locally Lipschitz and positive,

    integral_S |grad_X B| dm
      =kappa integral_S |grad_X L|/L dm
      =(1/N)sum_a e_a |c_a|/L_a
      <=Delta/(N r_s).                               (4)

All equalities are volume-a.e.; PL interfaces have zero volume unless they
are whole-fiber ties, in which case the coincident restrictions have the same
continuous gradient.

Normalization gives integral B dm=0. Since
B_-=(kappa log L)_+<=kappa log L_max and L_max>=1,

    integral_S |B| dm=2 integral_S B_- dm
         <=2M kappa log L_max
         =(2Delta/N)log L_max.                       (5)

Equations (4)--(5) prove a full-fiber W^(1,1) bound with an explicit small
constant. Neither is a surface martingale identity.

## 3. Uniform trace inequality, including nonsmooth fibers

If B(o,r_b) is contained in a convex K contained in B(0,R), every regular
boundary point X has

    n_K(X).(X-o)>=r_b,  |X-o|<=2R.

For a Lipschitz scalar function b on a neighborhood of K, Gauss--Green
applied to (X-o)|b(X)| gives

    r_b integral_boundary(K) |b| dS
       <=d integral_K |b| dX+2R integral_K |grad b| dX. (6)

The chain rule for |b| holds a.e. One can also obtain (6) by smoothing the
Lipschitz function and passing by dominated convergence. Convex-body
boundaries are Lipschitz locally and their exceptional nonsmooth points are
surface-null, so no smoothness of K is required. In d=1, dS counts the two
endpoints, and (6) is the ordinary fundamental-theorem estimate.

At each positive finite-PL pair, B=-kappa log L is Lipschitz on a fixed
neighborhood of that body's compact hull. Its Lipschitz constant need not be
uniform: (4) is the uniform integral bound actually used. Sum (6) over z and
use (4)--(5):

    integral_boundary(S) |B| dS
       <=Delta/(N r_b) [2d log L_max+2R/r_s]
       <=epsilon S_max/(N r_b)
            [2d(log H+N log(1/epsilon))+2R/r_s].       (7)

In particular the TOTAL VARIATION of the scaled logarithmic surface measure

    -[Delta/(NM)] log L dS

tends to zero, at rate O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)). This includes both signs;
there is no residual positive entropy measure in this same-certificate,
uniform-source-core limit.

The proof does not identify the independent surface and volume couplings.
It uses their shared coefficient only through the explicit volume identity
(2) and an ordinary trace inequality.

## 4. Consequence for the actual physical density

The audited common dual has the exact density

    Xi_z(X)=W_z(X)-beta
      +sum_(a:p_a=z) e_a P_a(X)^(-N)/(N E_a)
      +(1/(2M))sum_i e_i sum_j rho_ij
                      [u_ij.(X-g_z)]^2
      -(N+2)Delta/(2NM)+B(z,X).                       (8)

Here W is the SAME inward cap selector, including consistent supporting
allocations and any atomic whole-fiber selectors; 0<=W<=1. The cap normals
are normalized by u^T Sigma u=1, rho_ij sum to one, sum_i e_i=Delta,
P_a is the source energy denominator, and E_a the own energy.

The source ball gives E_a>=E_*:=omega_d r_s^d, by energy inclusion
monotonicity at its center. The optimal denominator has P_a>=1/N on K_p.
Also |u_ij|<=lambda_*^(-1/2), |X-g_z|<=2R. Surface areas are uniformly
bounded: the same support-distance divergence calculation gives

    S:=sum_z surface(K_z)<=dM/r_b<=S_*.

Writing S_f,* for an upper bound on an individual fiber area, the total
variation of every non-logarithmic correction in (8) is at most

    Delta C_*,
    C_* = N^(N-1) S_f,*/E_*
           +2R^2 S_*/(M_* lambda_*)
           +(N+2)S_*/(2N M_*).                       (9)

Thus

    integral_boundary |Xi-(W-beta)| dS
         <=Delta C_*+integral_boundary |B| dS
         =O(epsilon log(1/epsilon)).                 (10)

For every actual test speed v in the SAME addable physical cone,

    integral_boundary (W-beta)v dS
       <=||v||_infinity [Delta C_*+integral_boundary |B| dS]. (11)

This is a uniform approximate unbuffered action inequality for bounded
speeds. It is not a cap-payment estimate. In particular it does not assert
that W is a freely chosen closed-cap indicator or that the limiting cap
directions have any additional regularity.

If the bodies converge and the cone includes every fixed globally finite
convex function Phi(z,X) as a signed physical speed, pass to a subsequence
of W dS. Physical boundary measures dS converge weakly to those of the
limiting fibers, so W dS converges to w_0 dS_0 with 0<=w_0<=1. Then

    integral Phi (w_0-beta_0) dS_0<=0                 (12)

for every such Phi. Affine Phi and their negatives give equal mass and
first moments. This is only the resulting boundary convex-order stress.
It does not provide Gamma, a common-template allocation, or a new
identification of volume and surface transport.

For completeness, physical boundary-measure convergence here follows by
using a common interior radial center in each converging fiber. Their convex
gauges converge uniformly and their gradients converge a.e. at
differentiability points of the limit gauge. The radial surface Jacobian is
rho^(d-1)/(n.e); the common inball and outer radius bound its denominator
away from zero. Dominated convergence gives the asserted weak convergence,
also with the unit normal recorded. The d=1 assertion is endpoint convergence.

## 5. The weaker parallel-motion probe and its exact scope

Common inner and outer parallel families are actual compatible families:

    K_z^-(t)=K_z minus_inner t B_d,
    K_z^+(t)=K_z+t B_d.

For an anchored relation q=sum lambda_i z_i, if X_i belongs to K_zi^-(t),
then sum lambda_i X_i+tB_d is contained in sum lambda_i K_zi, hence in K_q.
For the outer family use sum lambda_i tB_d=tB_d. Both families remain
positive for small t and their canonical hull has exactly those sampled
fibers. This is already archived, for example in
`candidate f324bc23ceb65e89`.

Here is the nonsmooth weighted first-variation proof. Translate an inball
center to zero and write the radial function rho(e). Inner and outer
parallel bodies have radial functions given by the infimum of

    [h_K(u) minus_or_plus t]/(u.e),  u.e>0.

At a regular old radial endpoint the minimizing normal is unique.
Minimizers for small t have u.e bounded away from zero by the fixed inner
and outer radii, and every limit is that old normal. Comparing the old and
new minimizers gives

    (rho_minus(t,e)-rho(e))/t -> -1/(n.e),
    (rho_plus(t,e)-rho(e))/t  ->  1/(n.e).

Homothetic inner/outer bounds give a uniform dominating radial speed.
Polar integration therefore yields, for each continuous weight psi,

    d/dt|0 integral_Kminus(t) psi=-integral_boundary(K) psi dS,
    d/dt|0 integral_Kplus(t) psi= integral_boundary(K) psi dS. (13)

Thus their inward normal speeds are respectively +1 and -1 surface-a.e.
No continuity is asserted for an indicator at a supporting cap facet:
those fixed-cap responses use the already audited directional selectors.

If v=1 alone is included in the same dual, (8) only proves

    integral B_+ dS
      <=[beta+(N+2)kappa/2]S+integral B_- dS.          (14)

If both parallel motions belong to the common tested cone, linearity of
the selected dual gives integral Xi dS=0. This is an exact total surface
mass identity, not an assertion that individual supporting-cap losses are
linear in the signed speed. Their common selector was obtained before
using that linear identity.

Equation (14), even together with log normalization, would not by itself
prove (7). The missing input is exactly the source-gradient identity (4).

## 6. A separate convex-threshold bound

Suppose the SAME physical cone tests every finite convex potential. Put

    C_0=beta+(N+2)kappa/2.

The non-logarithmic positive terms in (8), including W, are nonnegative,
so Xi>=B-C_0. The function B has a globally finite convex extension: extend
-kappa log s below a positive minimum of the finitely many A_r on a common
compact neighborhood by its tangent line, and take the maximum of the
resulting convex functions of A_r. It agrees with B on that neighborhood.
Consequently Phi=(B-C_0)_+ is an admissible finite convex inward speed.

    0>=integral Xi Phi dS>=integral Phi^2 dS.

It follows that B<=C_0 on every sampled boundary, first surface-a.e. and
then everywhere by continuity and full support of convex-body surface
measure. Convexity gives the same bound throughout every sampled fiber.
In particular

    L>=exp[-beta/kappa-(N+2)/2] on S.                 (15)

The potential is an actual compatible motion: define each new fiber by
u.X+t Phi(z,X)<=h_Kz(u) for all unit u. Convexity of Phi and the old
anchored support inequalities preserve all anchored inclusions. It is
nested, remains positive for small t, and has speed Phi at regular old
boundary points. Finite actual speed addition and compactness of the
selector dual justify testing an entire class before choosing the final
dual. One must not choose an arbitrary separator for a smaller test class
and then silently require it to satisfy this additional test.

This useful pointwise bound is weaker than the vanishing statement (7)
for the present limit question. It neither supplies nor replaces the
uniform-source-core hypothesis in (4).

## 7. Exact warning against discarding the source certificate

On the actual interval K=[-1,1], put a_m=2^(-m), kappa_m=1/m, and

    J(a)=[(2+a)log(2+a)-a log a-2]/2,
    L_m(x)=exp[-J(a_m)](x+1+a_m),
    B_m(x)=[J(a_m)-log(x+1+a_m)]/m.

These are positive affine log-normalized parameters. Their maxima remain
bounded, integral_K B_m=0, and B_m tends uniformly to zero on every compact
subset of (-1,1]. Yet, with endpoint-counting surface measure,

    B_m(-1)->log 2,  B_m(1)->0,
    integral_boundary(K) |B_m| ->log 2,
    integral_K |B_m'|=[log(2+a_m)-log a_m]/m ->log 2.

Thus the source-gradient estimate (4) genuinely rules out an otherwise
possible convex boundary layer. This family is NOT asserted to possess
the same physical/volume certificate with uniformly interior sources,
to be a joint minimum, or to refute the theorem. Its last displayed limit
shows explicitly why it cannot satisfy (4) with Delta=O(1/m) and fixed r_s.

## 8. Scope

The new conclusion is the total-variation vanishing of the SAME physical
logarithmic boundary term and the approximate action inequality (11).
All supporting selections and multiple source contacts remain intact.
The argument does not require smooth fibers, cap regularity, an optimizer
derivative, a uniform PL slope bound, or a uniform boundary bound for log L
itself. The resulting limiting physical stress still requires a separate
geometric cap-payment argument; the mixed centerpoint bound is not proved.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_scaled_surface_log_trace_defect_transport.py` checks
the scalar coefficients, exact weighted box first variations, and the
normalization/gradient formulas in the boundary-layer warning. These are
algebra and concrete-body checks; the general convergence statements are
proved above, not inferred from the checker.
